additional_functions_note: getEarnedYield(_self,_ctx) (same CDP library) is load-bearing: its deterministic yield computation (accumulated-weight delta times totalDeposited, decoded) fixes the concrete _earnedYield value that (a) selects which branch of the if/else executes and (b) feeds directly into the totalCredit assignment in the taken branch; counted atomically per §6, not itemized.
external_spec_note: All dependencies are local source (same-library call to getEarnedYield) or generic language/library semantics (SafeMath .sub() revert-on-underflow) — no protocol/business convention beyond the source is needed to justify the selected relation. The intended accumulate-not-overwrite behavior is additionally corroborated in-source by the sibling view function getUpdatedTotalCredit, which computes _self.totalCredit + (yield - debt) — no external protocol spec needed to establish it.
case_notes: SafeMath's .sub() (used on _earnedYield.sub(_currentTotalDebt) in the taken if-branch, and on _self.totalDebt.sub(_earnedYield) in the untaken else branch) is a generic, protocol-independent overflow/underflow-checked arithmetic primitive — load-bearing where it's actually on the derivation path but excluded from the numeric counts per §6 Step 2 (generic library-semantics dependency, not protocol-specific).
extraction_note: Independently re-derived R1-1–R1-7 and RQ2-A from the case JSON's own code entries; matches README §4 R1-4's own reference to this exact case (CDP.update's patch totalCredit += delta ending up Post/Entry-Exit, not During-equality) and the Code4rena report (56.md, H-02: 'CDP.sol update overwrites user's credit on every positive increment', sponsor-confirmed). Relevant-statements set = {_earnedYield = _self.getEarnedYield(_ctx); if(_earnedYield > _self.totalDebt); _currentTotalDebt = _self.totalDebt; _self.totalCredit = _earnedYield.sub(_currentTotalDebt)}. Excluded: `_self.totalDebt = 0;` (redefines totalDebt but does not feed the totalCredit derivation chain — _currentTotalDebt was already captured on the prior line), the untaken else-branch statement `_self.totalDebt = _self.totalDebt.sub(_earnedYield);` (does not write totalCredit and is not on the debug-seeded scenario's taken path), and the trailing `_self.lastAccumulatedYieldWeight = _ctx.accumulatedYieldWeight;` (unrelated to totalCredit). _ctx judged not an independently countable unique value (used only to pass through to the atomic getEarnedYield call, no independent role in the relation's own arithmetic) — a judgment call, noted here for transparency. Under the case's own @Debugging seed (totalCredit=[1000,1000], totalDebt=[0,0], totalDeposited=[1000,1000], lastAccumulatedYieldWeight.x=[1e18,1e18], accumulatedYieldWeight.x=[1.2e18,1.2e18]), getEarnedYield evaluates to 200, so the if-branch is taken and totalCredit is overwritten to 200 — the annotation's Entry(1000) <= Exit(200) is false (1000 <= 200 fails), correctly flagging the reported overwrite-instead-of-accumulate defect; under the patched fix totalCredit would be 1000+200=1200, satisfying Entry(1000) <= Exit(1200). Value-vs-Algorithm judgment call: classified Value-level because the delta computation itself (_earnedYield.sub(_currentTotalDebt)) is fully present and correct — the buggy code is missing exactly one additive operand (the prior _self.totalCredit term) from what should be a two-term sum, i.e. an operator-level defect (assignment `=` standing in for accumulation `+=`) within an otherwise-complete expression, which the methodology's own §5 text explicitly lists (operand/operator/constant) as Value-level; an Algorithm-level reading (treating the missing accumulation as a wholly separate missing processing step, analogous to a missing normalization pass) was considered and rejected because no distinct additional computational step is absent — only the second addend of an otherwise-intact sum.
